Following are points made by two or more reviewers with our collective response to each. Note that some points relate more to the proposed legislation than to the draft environmental statement.
Commitment. 'The earlier draft of the EIS states, under the "Commitment" section that, "The methods employed to reach this goal (protection, conservation and propagation of a renewable resource) will not require the irreversible or irretrievable commitment of natural resources." Several comments were received questioning or disputing this statement. The Washington Department of Ecology asks for further explanation, and the Environmental Defense Fund calls the same statement, "not clear." The Washington Department of Game contends that there are committments of resources -- "Most obvious are land and water; in some instances certain species which have been displaced by endangered forms will suffer a reduction in range and loss in total population size." The State of Arizona and the U.S. Bureau of Outdoor Recreation point out a third dimension to commitment that we had not considered in the earlier EIS. BOR says that, "natural resources, such as cultivated crops and forest products, become partially irretrievable when they are not harvested." Arizona points out in regard to the commitment of lands for endangered species habitat, "The concept of land or any other resource is meaningless unless viewed in relation to time. In the case of habitat an acre-year would be the appropriate unit to evaluate the nature of the commitment in terms of irretrievability. Certainly, any acre-years consumed as a result of the program would be irretrievable." As a result, the "Commitment" section has been rewritten to include time as a resource, and to account for animals displaced by restored endangered species.
